answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a stake locked on a public mesa of attestations: an agent proves its work history before it can draw nectar from shared pools, and the stake is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities. A hollow identity with no history and no stake gets no access, so an attacker must pay the full stake cost for every fake agent — the cost of flooding the network scales linearly with the number of fakes, while honest agents pay once.
